description: Add AI tooling support so AURA Copilot can programmatically modify CRM schemas. Define tool schemas that Qwen/other LLMs can call to add/update/delete fields and stages. This enables the AI to propose schema evolution (e.g., 'I notice you need an Escalation field; adding it now'). All tool calls are validated server-side before execution.
steps: Define AI tool schemas in backend/app/services/ai_tools.py: Create CRMSchemaTools class with static methods: add_crm_field(), update_crm_field(), delete_crm_field(), add_crm_stage(), update_crm_stage(), delete_crm_stage(). Each method maps to the corresponding backend endpoint from FEAT-002.

Create tool definitions in OpenAI function-calling format in backend/app/services/ai_tools.py: Define COPILOT_TOOLS list with JSON schemas for each tool. Include descriptions, parameters (with types, min/max, enums), and required fields. Ensure schemas match the request/response contracts from FEAT-002.

Create tool execution endpoint in backend/app/routers/copilot.py (or appropriate file): POST /api/v1/copilot/tool-call or similar. Accepts tool_call payload with tool_name and parameters. Validates authenticated user, maps tool_name to CRMSchemaTools method, executes with user context, returns result or error.
Add authorization checks in tool execution: Every tool call must verify user owns the CRM being modified. Use the same authorization pattern as FEAT-002 endpoints.
Add input validation in tool execution: Validate parameters with Pydantic before passing to CRMSchemaTools. Reject invalid tool names, missing required parameters, out-of-range values.

Implement tool result formatting: Copilot tools return success/error responses compatible with OpenAI function-calling format. Success includes updated CRMConfiguration. Error includes error code and message.

Add tests in backend/tests/test_copilot_tools.py: test_add_field_via_tool(), test_update_field_via_tool(), test_unauthorized_user_cannot_call_tool(), test_invalid_parameters_rejected(), test_tool_result_format_valid()

Update copilot system prompt in backend/app/services/ollama_provider.py to include COPILOT_TOOLS in available functions. Ensure prompt instructs Qwen to call tools only when the user asks for schema modifications.
Document tool schemas in docs/API_CONTRACTS.md: Add section describing available Copilot tools, their parameters, and expected responses
acceptance_criteria: CRMSchemaTools class exists with 6 static methods (add_field, update_field, delete_field, add_stage, update_stage, delete_stage)
COPILOT_TOOLS list contains valid OpenAI function-calling tool schemas
POST /api/v1/copilot/tool-call endpoint accepts and executes tool calls
All tool calls verify user owns the CRM (403 if unauthorized)
Invalid parameters rejected with 400 or 422 error
Successful tool execution returns updated CRMConfiguration
Tool calls increment configuration_version (via backend endpoints)
Copilot system prompt includes tool definitions
Qwen can be instructed to call tools to modify schema
verification: Run: cd backend && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_copilot_tools.py -v (verify tool tests pass)
Manual test: Call POST /api/v1/copilot/tool-call with add_field tool → field added to CRM
Manual test: Call tool without CRM ownership → 403 Forbidden
Manual test: Call tool with invalid parameters → 400 or 422 with error message
Manual test: Prompt Copilot with 'Add an Escalation field to my CRM' → Copilot calls add_crm_field tool, field appears in CRM
findings: FEAT-002 must complete first (backend endpoints that tools will call). The CRMSchemaTools methods will mostly delegate to the PATCH/POST/DELETE endpoints from FEAT-002, so this feature is lightweight once FEAT-002 is done. The main work is mapping tools to OpenAI function-calling format and updating the Copilot system prompt.
